summary.headline: News-release and article pages carry zero JSON-LD structured data -- no NewsArticle/Article node naming headline, author or date -- despite the homepage itself carrying a well-formed Organization/WebSite graph — high severity, Extend the site's existing structured-data generation (visible on the homepage) to press-release and news-article templates, adding a NewsArticle node with headline, datePublished, dateModified and author.

findings.title: News-release and article pages carry zero JSON-LD structured data -- no NewsArticle/Article node naming headline, author or date -- despite the homepage itself carrying a well-formed Organization/WebSite graph
findings.evidence: The homepage (https://www.nasa.gov/) has a real, well-formed JSON-LD @graph (Organization, WebSite with a SearchAction, an ImageObject for the NASA logo, a WebPage node) -- structured data investment clearly exists on this site. But all four sampled press-release/news pages (/news-release/saturns-rings-shine-in-hubbles-latest-portrait/, /news-release/artemis-testing-at-plum-brook-station/, /news-release/experience-high-res-science-in-first-8k-footage-from-space/, /news-release/nasa-invites-media-to-talk-to-small-satellite-experts-tour-labs/) contain zero JSON-LD blocks of any kind -- 0/4. This is the content type where Article/NewsArticle markup matters most: headline, author, and publish date are exactly the facts a NewsArticle node exists to state unambiguously, and this site's own homepage proves the underlying schema-generation capability is present, just not applied to the pages carrying the actual news content.

reproduction.observed: 0 on every one of the four sampled article pages; 1 (a real Organization/WebSite graph) on the homepage
reproduction.expected: A NewsArticle node per article stating headline, datePublished, author and publisher, consistent with the schema-generation already present on the homepage

suggested_action.summary: Extend the site's existing structured-data generation (visible on the homepage) to press-release and news-article templates, adding a NewsArticle node with headline, datePublished, dateModified and author.
suggested_action.mechanism: An assistant asked about a specific NASA finding or announcement has no structured source to confirm the headline, date or authorship of the claim, and must fall back to unreliable prose extraction from a page that -- as a separate finding on this same site shows -- does not reliably state its own publish date in any form.
steps: Add NewsArticle JSON-LD to the press-release and news-article page templates, populated from the same CMS fields already driving the visible headline and byline.
Verify the schema-generation logic already used on the homepage is reusable rather than needing to be rebuilt for article templates.
suggested_action.verification: A sample of article pages each contain a NewsArticle node whose headline and date match the page's own visible content.

findings.title: News-release pages carry no reliable publish-date signal in any form -- no JSON-LD date, no article:published_time meta tag, no <time> element -- and the one date-like signal present appears to be a bulk migration timestamp rather than genuine per-article freshness
findings.evidence: All four sampled press-release pages have zero <time> elements, no article:published_time meta tag, and (per the companion structured-data finding) no JSON-LD datePublished. The only date-like signal present on any of them is og:updated_time -- but all four values cluster within three hours of each other on the same calendar day (2023-07-26T12:08:12, 14:47:34, 15:13:20 and 15:27:13, all -04:00) despite the four articles covering unrelated events. That clustering is far more consistent with a one-time platform migration or template re-save stamping every legacy page with the same timestamp than with genuine, independent editorial updates -- meaning even this one present signal would mislead a reader or assistant into treating a years-old release as recently touched. For content whose entire value is 'is this the latest finding or old news' -- exactly the question space-and-science journalism lives in -- this leaves no trustworthy way to answer it.

reproduction.observed: og:updated_time values across four unrelated articles all fall within a 3-hour window on 2023-07-26, and no other date signal exists anywhere on the page
reproduction.expected: A datePublished (JSON-LD) or article:published_time meta tag reflecting the article's actual original release date, distinct from any bulk technical timestamp

suggested_action.summary: Add a genuine, per-article datePublished signal (JSON-LD and/or article:published_time) sourced from the CMS's original publish record, not from the last template re-save or migration event.
suggested_action.mechanism: Without a trustworthy date, an assistant cannot tell a reader whether a NASA finding is current or years old, and cannot correctly caveat older claims -- a real risk specifically for fast-moving space/science topics where the same headline pattern ('Hubble captures...') recurs across many different years.
steps: Confirm the CMS stores each release's original publish date distinct from its last-modified/migration timestamp.
Expose the original publish date as JSON-LD datePublished and/or an article:published_time meta tag, keeping dateModified/og:updated_time separate and accurate.
Spot-check that dateModified values are not still clustered around the same migration event once fixed.
suggested_action.verification: A sample of article pages' JSON-LD datePublished values are distinct, plausible dates matching the article's actual subject matter and byline era, not a single shared timestamp.

opportunities.title: Publish an llms.txt given the site's existing schema-generation investment shows real machine-readability intent
opportunities.rationale: No llms.txt exists (a genuine 404, not a soft-404 shell). Given NASA's content is public-domain, high-value, and already has partial structured-data investment on the homepage, a short llms.txt pointing to key entry points (missions, news releases, STEM content, image galleries) would be a low-cost extension of that existing intent.
opportunities.mechanism: A documented entry-point index helps a well-behaved agent navigate a large, multi-section government site more efficiently than relying on sitemap discovery alone.
steps: Add a minimal llms.txt listing the major content sections (missions, news, STEM, multimedia).

not_assessed.check: Answerability -- question-coverage, definitional clarity, quotable-fact density, question-shaped structure (answerability-audit)
not_assessed.reason: This run hand-verified two specific mechanisms (missing article-level structured data and missing publish-date signals) rather than running the full sampled-page probe. The article text itself reads as substantive, well-written science journalism on direct inspection, but no systematic question-coverage derivation was performed.
not_assessed.impact: Cannot state a coverage percentage or list specific unanswered questions for nasa.gov; this is a gap in this run, not a claim that the site's prose fails or passes this check.

not_assessed.check: Off-site corroboration and entity ambiguity (freshness-corroboration-audit, checks 4-5)
not_assessed.reason: Not performed in this run to stay within the demonstration's time budget.
not_assessed.impact: Not a meaningful concern for an entity as unambiguous and widely corroborated as NASA, but genuinely not checked.

not_assessed.check: On-site engagement -- LCP/CLS/TBT, above-the-fold content, interaction affordances (engagement-audit)
not_assessed.reason: No headless-browser engine (Playwright/Puppeteer) was available in this run's environment.
not_assessed.impact: Cannot assess the actual on-site experience for a JavaScript-executing visitor.

not_assessed.check: JS-dependency ratio and image-locked-facts check across a full stratified sample (render-extractability-audit)
not_assessed.reason: This run hand-verified four press-release pages plus the homepage, all of which delivered substantial real text without JavaScript execution -- a clean result on every page tried -- rather than running discover_pages.py's seeded sampling across the full site (missions, images-of-the-day, STEM content).
not_assessed.impact: The clean result is well-corroborated across the pages actually tried, but a broader sample might surface JS-dependent sections (e.g. interactive mission trackers or 3D visualizations) not checked here.
